Applied AI Engineer - Direct Acquisition
 Hybrid in London, UK
 We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join the Direct Acquisition team. 
 You'll design and build AI agents that run whole business processes, from planning the work to learning from the results. What you find will steer how far iwoca takes agents across the business.
 The company 
 Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don't wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that's as flexible and responsive as they are.
 That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.
 We've already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £5 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.
 The team 
 Direct Acquisition includes iwoca's Marketing, Sales, Brand and Acquisition Tech teams. Together, they reach UK businesses of all shapes and sizes through paid and organic marketing channels and direct sales.
 A new team in Direct Acquisition builds agents that automate and improve acquisition processes. That's its only focus, and it works closely with Acquisition Tech. It's small – a product owner and you – and everyone builds. You'll report to the Head of Direct Acquisition, who sets the commercial direction.
 The role 
 As the Applied AI Engineer, you'll build the agents and the systems around them. Most of the work is system design and backend engineering.
 You'll start with direct mail. The first goal is an agent that plans each monthly round, uses iwoca's existing predictive models to build the mailing file, and learns from the results as they come in. The pattern is simple to say and hard to get right: the agent orchestrates, deterministic code does the work, and a human in the loop approves the file before it goes to print. You'll work with the people who run each process to understand the edge cases, and with Core Systems and Compliance on access and controls.
 The agents don't exist yet, and much is still open: which processes the team takes on, and what the architecture looks like. You'll own those design decisions and write most of the code yourself, much of it with AI coding tools. Some of this won't work, and finding out why is one of the main outputs of the role.
 Architecture. You'll design what agents need to run reliably: memory that persists between runs, task management, access to tools, permissions, and a record of every decision and why. You'll build each piece so the next process can reuse it.
 Guardrails. You'll decide where the agent uses judgement and where code enforces rules the agent can't change, like suppressions, compliance checks and budget limits.
 Delivery. You'll own each agent end to end: connect it to iwoca's predictive models, data pipelines and channel tools, and run it alongside the current process until it has shown it works.
 Measurement. You'll track how often agents need a person, where they fail, what they cost, and what they're worth.
 The requirements 
 We're looking for the depth of someone who has solved hard problems, and the pace of someone who moves fast in areas that are new to them.
 Essential:
 System ownership. You've owned a complex system end to end, from design to running it in production, and lived with the consequences of your architecture choices.
 Design judgement. You've made architecture decisions other people built on, and you can explain the trade-offs and what you'd change. When an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.
 Pace. You've got things live quickly in unfamiliar areas and they kept working once people relied on them.
 Agent engineering. You've built systems where LLMs take actions – more than chat or summaries – and you can explain what went wrong and how you fixed it. You know when a problem needs an agent and when it needs a for-loop.
 Controls. You've built permissions, data access rules and audit trails into systems from the start.
 Constructive challenge. You work well with commercial and product colleagues, and when an idea won't work, you say so and offer a better one.
 AI leverage. You've used AI coding tools to produce engineering work you couldn't have delivered without them – a service, an integration, or an internal tool others use. You have opinions on how to get the most out of them, and you check their output before it reaches production.
 Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.
 Bonus:
 Languages and data tools. You've worked with Python, Go, Snowflake or dbt.
 Evaluation. You've built evals that measure how an agent performs and where it fails.
 Marketing and growth tech. You've worked with ad platforms, CRMs or direct mail.
 Quantitative foundations. You come from a numerical or technical field, such as physics, engineering, maths or computer science.
 The salary 
 We expect to pay from £80,000 to £120,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.
 The culture 
 At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.
 We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.
 The offices 
 We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:
 Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.
 Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.
 The benefits 
 Flexible working hours.
 Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.
 A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.
 25 days' holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.
 A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.
 Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.
 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.
 An employee equity incentive scheme.
 Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.
 Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.
 Two company retreats a year: we've been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.
 And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:
 A learning and development budget for everyone.
 Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.
 Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

 Research Assistant - Software Security & Program Analysis (anywhere in Germany)
 The Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft ( www.fraunhofer.com ) is one of the world's leading organizations for application-oriented research. 74 institutes develop pioneering technologies for our economy and society – more precisely: 30 000 people from technology, science, administration and IT. They know: Anyone who comes to Fraunhofer wants to and can make a difference. For themselves, for us and for the markets of today and tomorrow.
 Increasing digitalization makes software security a key prerequisite for trust, resilience, and innovation. This is precisely where we come in.
 The National Research Center for Applied Cybersecurity ATHENE is a joint institution of the Fraunhofer Society with the participation of Fraunhofer SIT, Fraunhofer IGD, TU Darmstadt, and Darmstadt University of Applied Sciences. In a unique cooperation model, we combine cutting-edge university and non-university research in the field of cybersecurity.
 Fraunhofer SIT is one of the leading research institutions for IT and software security in Germany and Europe. Our focus is not on classic software development, but on the analysis, evaluation, and securing of software.
 Be part of change 
 You will work on applied research projects in the field of software security in cooperation with our partners in academic institutions, industry, and public administration
 Development and scientific evaluation of new methods for detecting, analyzing, verifying, and fixing software vulnerabilities
 Research into novel methods of static and dynamic program analysis, including fuzzing and the use of AI methods for vulnerability detection
 Security analyses of real software systems, including:
 Code reviews
 Penetration tests and security assessments
 Risk and threat analyses
 Collaboration in publicly funded research projects and industry collaborations
 Preparation of project reports and scientific publications
 Presentation of research results at national and international confer
 What you contribute 
 Completed university degree (master's) in computer science, IT security, or a related discipline
 Strong interest in software security, program analysis, and security research with a focus on software-driven systems
 Very good programming skills (e.g., Java, C/C++), with a particular focus on code-level security
 Experience or interest in one or more of the following areas:
 Static/dynamic program analysis, fuzzing
 Pentesting, exploit analysis, vulnerability research
 Risk/threat modeling
 Code reviews and penetration testing
 Very good written and spoken German and English skills
 What we offer 
 Collaboration at a renowned, internationally leading institute in the field of cybersecurity
 Support for your own scientific and professional development in the field of software security, including support for a doctoral project
 Friendly, open, and collegial working environment with a dynamic and creative working atmosphere
 Family-friendly work culture with flexible working conditions (various working time models, flexible working locations and hours, mobile working, job ticket subsidy, support services through the pme family service, etc.)
 Company pension plan, capital-forming benefits, deferred compensation
 Conveniently located (Darmstadt main station within walking distance in approx. 10 minutes), free parking and efficient charging infrastructure for electric vehicles with preferential conditions for employees, alternatively a centrally located office in Heilbronn
 The weekly working time is 39 hours. This position is also available on a part-time basis. We value and promote the diversity of our employees' skills and therefore welcome all applications – regardless of age, gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, ideology, disability, sexual orientation and identity. Severely disabled persons are given preference in the event of equal suitability. Our tasks are diverse and adaptable – for applicants with disabilities, we work together to find solutions that best promote their abilities. Appointment, remuneration and social security benefits based on the public-sector collective wage agreement (TVöD). Additionally Fraunhofer may grant performance-based variable remuneration components. 
 With its focus on developing key technologies that are vital for the future and enabling the commercial utilization of this work by business and industry, Fraunhofer plays a central role in the innovation process. As a pioneer and catalyst for groundbreaking developments and scientific excellence, Fraunhofer helps shape society now and in the future.  
 Ready for a change? Then apply now and make a difference! Once we have received your online application, you will receive an automatic confirmation of receipt. We will then get back to you as soon as possible and let you know what happens next.

We Are: 
 Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP integration, simulation and analysis solutions and design services., empowering the creation of high-performance silicon chips and software content. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 
 You Are: 
 You’re an early-career engineer eager to build semiconductor design infrastructure. You value rigorous digital design and enjoy improving tool flows as much as writing code. You understand that when a designer’s environment breaks, productivity drops and milestones slip—and you care. You think in systems, not just scripts, considering dependencies, data ownership, and failure modes before automating. You can debug Linux, Python, and EDA issues independently, knowing when a workaround is acceptable versus when to fix the root cause. You take initiative, ask questions, read documentation, and test safely before deploying changes. You are keen on improving productivity of design flow using latest available AI tools and methodology. At Synopsys, you’ll keep ASIC teams productive and accelerate silicon IP delivery. 
 What You'll Be Doing: 
 Develop and maintain infrastructure supporting daily ASIC design, verification, test and implementation workflows.
 Install, configure, upgrade, and manage EDA tools and licenses (simulation, synthesis, timing, etc.).
 Build and maintain automation for flow setup, job submission, tracking, data management, and reporting (Python/Tcl/Bash/Perl).
 Support compute and storage platforms: filesystem management, monitoring, and ensuring capacity/availability for large datasets.
 Support HPC/compute farms and schedulers: batch submissions, resource allocation, and job scheduling.
 Troubleshoot and proactively monitor environments (tool configs, permissions, paths, licenses), and maintain clear documentation for users.
 Work with the central methodology teams to test, deploy new design flows. Use AI tools/flow to improve the execution efficiency.
 The Impact You Will Have: 
 Keep ASIC design teams productive and on track for tapeout by ensuring infrastructure uptime and stability.
 Automate repetitive setup and flow tasks to save engineers significant time each week.
 Proactively monitor compute, storage, and licenses to prevent issues from blocking critical runs.
 Ensure compute farm and storage capacity scales smoothly during simulation/synthesis workload spikes.
 Deliver reliable updates, documentation, and self-serve processes that reduce troubleshooting and prevent downstream failures.
 What You'll Need: 
 Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
 0-2 years of experience in software development, scripting, IT infrastructure, or engineering support roles.
 Proficiency in at least one scripting language such as Python, Tcl, Bash, or Perl.
 Working knowledge of Linux operating systems and command-line tools.
 Ability to read technical materials, follow procedures, and learn new tools independently.
 Exposure to ASIC design flows, EDA tools, or semiconductor engineering environments is a plus.
 Familiarity with compute farms, HPC environments, or large-scale storage systems is a plus.
 Experience with configuration management or release processes is a plus.
 Some experience of AI tools/flow is an added plus.
 Who You Are: 
 Proactive problem solver, comfortable with ambiguity and rapid change.
 R&D mindset engineer someone who can troubleshoot issues end-to-end by reproducing failures, checking logs, and isolating tool vs. environment vs. user causes.
 Collaborative team player who communicates clearly with engineers, explaining problems like license failures without blame.
 Problem solver. Writes robust automation with logging and error handling to handle real-world usage and edge cases.
 Detail-oriented and highly organized. Creates clear, beginner-friendly documentation that enables self-service and consistent execution. Stays organized and proactive: track tasks, provide status updates, and escalate blockers early to keep workflows reliable.
 The Team You'll Be Part Of 
 You will join a team at Synopsys that builds and supports the infrastructure powering daily ASIC design and verification. You’ll collaborate with CAD/IT and R&D IP engineering teams to maintain EDA tool environments, automation, compute farms, and storage systems. The team values strong troubleshooting, clear documentation, and safe change management to keep workflows stable and teams on track for tapeout. 
 Rewards and Benefits: 
 We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

items.jobTitle: Doktorandin / Doktorand (m/w/d) Physik, Elektrotechnik, Supraleitung, Optoelektronik (26-189-2B)
items.jobDescription:
English version below: 
 Messkunst „Made in Germany" – dafür stehen die ca. 2100 Mitarbeitenden der Physikalisch-Technischen Bundesanstalt (PTB). Als nationales Metrologieinstitut und führende Forschungseinrichtung entwickeln wir in einem internationalen Arbeitsumfeld weltweit führende Standards für das Messen. So sorgen wir dafür, dass Menschen und Organisationen Messungen vertrauen können.
 In Braunschweig suchen wir Sie für den Fachbereich 2.4 „Quantenelektronik“ als:
 Doktorandin / Doktorand (m/w/d) 
Physik, Elektrotechnik, Supraleitung, Optoelektronik 
 Entgeltgruppe 13 TVöD Bund ○ befristet für 3 Jahre ○ Teilzeit 33,15 Wochenstunden
 Ihre Aufgaben: 
 Im Rahmen eines Forschungsprojekts sollen neuartige Photodioden entwickelt, mit Supraleitungsschaltungen kombiniert und mit optoelektronischer Messtechnik bei kryogenen Temperaturen charakterisiert werden. Dazu steht in der PTB ein Reinraumzentrum (RRZ) mit umfangreicher Dünnschichttechnologie und entsprechende Aufbauten für kryogene optoelektronische Messungen zur Verfügung. Ihre Tätigkeiten beinhalten:
 Prozessentwicklung zum Abscheiden dünner supraleitender und normalleitender Schichten und deren Nanostrukturierung im RRZ der PTB
 Betrieb und Weiterentwicklung eines optoelektronischen Anrege-Abfrage-Experiments basierend auf Femtosekundenlasern
 Charakterisierung der im RRZ der PTB gefertigten Schaltungen mittels des optoelektronischen Aufbaus bei tiefen Temperaturen
 Präsentation und Publikation der wissenschaftlichen Ergebnisse
 Ihr Profil: 
 Hochschulstudium (Diplom/Master) der Fachrichtung Physik, Elektrotechnik oder vergleichbar mit mindestens „gutem“ Abschluss
 Praktische Erfahrungen in mindestens einem der folgenden Bereiche: Optoelektronik (insbes. mit Femtosekundenlasern), Dünnfilmtechnik, Nanostrukturierung, Kryoelektronik
 Programmiererfahrung, idealerweise in Python
 Experimentelles Geschick und analytische Fähigkeiten
 Hohes Maß an Engagement, eigenverantwortliches Arbeiten sowie Lernbereitschaft
 Englischkenntnisse (B2-Niveau) , Deutschkenntnisse sind von Vorteil
 Ausgeprägte Team- und Kommunikationsfähigkeit
 Bereitschaft zu Dienstreisen im In- und Ausland
 Die körperliche Eignung für Arbeiten im Reinraumzentrum und in einem Laserlabor wird vorausgesetzt (die Tätigkeit stellt besondere Anforderungen an Mobilität und Sehvermögen; wir prüfen jedoch im Einzelfall gerne Möglichkeiten der Anpassung)
 Wir bieten: 
 Nutzung moderner Forschungsinfrastruktur und hochpräziser Messtechnik
 Voller Fokus auf Ihre Promotion – ohne verpflichtende Lehrtätigkeit
 Individuelle Promotionsbetreuung sowie Unterstützung durch das Promovierendenprogramm der PTB
 Teilnahme an Fachkonferenzen und Aufbau wissenschaftlicher Netzwerke im nationalen und internationalen Umfeld
 Eine Übersicht unserer weiteren Benefits finden Sie auf unserer Karriereseite. 
 Das ist uns wichtig: 
 Die PTB fördert die Gleichstellung von Frauen und Männern und ist besonders an Bewerbungen von Frauen interessiert. Gleichzeitig sind wir bestrebt, die gesellschaftliche Vielfalt widerzuspiegeln. Daher ist jede Bewerbung, unabhängig von ihrem Geschlecht, ihrer kulturellen oder sozialen Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung oder sexuellen Identität herzlich willkommen. Schwerbehinderte oder ihnen gleichgestellte Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt berücksichtigt.
 Ihre Bewerbung: 
 Fachliche Fragen zu dieser Position beantwortet Ihnen im Fachbereich 2.4 : 
Dr. Mark Bieler, Tel.: 0531 592-2400, E-Mail: mark.bieler@ptb.de .
 Wir freuen uns auf Ihre Bewerbung bis zum 30. November 2026 unter der Kennziffer 26-189-2B. Bitte nutzen Sie dafür den Button „ONLINE BEWERBEN“ – dieser führt Sie direkt zu unserem Bewerbungsportal, wo Sie Ihre Unterlagen (Lebenslauf, Zeugnisse, Anschreiben) hochladen können. Bewerbungen per E-Mail können wir nicht berücksichtigen. Mit Ihrer Bewerbung akzeptieren Sie die Datenschutzbestimmungen .
 English version: 
 The art of measurement — made in Germany. Striving to perfect it is the mission of the 2,100 employees of PTB, the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt. As Germany’s national metrology institute and a leading center of research, we operate in an international environment to develop world-class measurement standards. We at PTB work to ensure that people and organizations can trust the measurements they use.
 At our Braunschweig site, we are looking to fill the following position in Department 2.4 “Quantum Electronics” as:
 PhD student (m/w/d) 
physics, electrical engineering, superconductivity, optoelectronics 
 Remuneration Group 13 TVöD Bund ○ Three-year fixed term ○ Part-time (33.15 hours/week)
 Your tasks: 
 As part of a research project, novel photodiodes are to be developed, combined with superconducting circuits and characterised using optoelectronic measurement techniques at cryogenic temperatures. To this end, the PTB has a cleanroom centre equipped with comprehensive thin-film technology and the necessary set-ups for cryogenic optoelectronic measurements. Your responsibilities will include:
 Process development for the deposition of thin superconducting and normal-conducting layers and their nanostructuring in PTB’s clean room center
 Operation and further development of an optoelectronic pump-probe experiment based on femtosecond lasers
 Characterisation of the circuits fabricated at PTB’s clean room center using the optoelectronic setup at low temperatures
 Presentation and publication of scientific results
 Your profile: 
 You have completed your university studies (German Diplom or Master’s) in physics, electrical engineering or a comparable subject and have obtained at least the grade good.
 Practical experience in at least one of the following areas: optoelectronics (particularly involving femtosecond lasers), thin-film technology, nanostructuring, cryoelectronics
 Programming experience, ideally in Python
 Experimental and analytical skills
 High level of commitment, ability to work independently, and willingness to learn
 Strong teamwork and communication skills
 German (B1 level) and English (B2 level) language skills
 Willingness to travel domestically and internationally
 Physical fitness for work in the cleanroom centre and laser laboratory is a prerequisite (the role places particular demands on mobility and eyesight; however, we are happy to explore options for adaptation on a case-by-case basis)
 We offer: 
 You can find an overview of our benefits on our careers page .
 This is important to us: 
 PTB promotes gender equality and strongly encourages applications from female candidates. At the same time, we strive to reflect the diversity of our society. We therefore welcome every application submitted, regardless of the candidate’s gender, cultural or social background, religion, ideology or sexual identity. If equally suited to the position, disabled persons or persons having equivalent status under German law will be given preference.
 Your application: 
 For subject-related questions concerning this position, please contact Department 2.4 : 
Dr. Mark Bieler, phone: +49 531 592-2400, email: mark.bieler@ptb.de .
 We look forward to receiving your application by 30 November 2026 under Ref. No. 26-189-2B. Please click on the following button: ONLINE BEWERBEN. This will directly lead you to our application portal where you can upload your documents (CV, certificates, Cover letter). Unfortunately, we cannot accept applications sent via email. With your application you accept the data protection regulations .

RLI is a non-profit research institute in Berlin. UNSER HERZ SCHLÄGT FÜR BILDUNG. 
 Du möchtest dein technisches Know-how weitergeben und Menschen auf ihrem Weg in den deutschen Arbeitsmarkt begleiten? In unserer Anpassungsqualifizierung unterstützt du beruflich qualifizierte Fachkräfte aus dem Ausland dabei, ihre vorhandenen Kompetenzen an die Anforderungen des deutschen Berufslebens anzupassen. Dabei verbindest du praxisnahe Wissensvermittlung mit moderner Fahrzeugtechnik und leistest einen wichtigen Beitrag zur beruflichen Integration unserer Teilnehmenden.
 DEINE AUFGABEN. 
 In dieser Rolle begleitest du internationale Fachkräfte bei ihrer fachlichen Weiterentwicklung und bereitest sie gezielt auf den beruflichen Einsatz in Deutschland vor. Du sorgst für eine praxisnahe, wertschätzende und erfolgreiche Lernerfahrung. Mit deinem Fachwissen schaffst du die Grundlage für nachhaltige berufliche Perspektiven.
 Du planst, gestaltest und führst theoretischen sowie praktischen Unterricht in der Kfz-Mechatronik mit Schwerpunkt PKW-Technik durch.
 Die fachliche und pädagogische Begleitung der Teilnehmenden gehört ebenso zu deinem Verantwortungsbereich wie die individuelle Lernunterstützung bei unterschiedlichen Vorkenntnissen und Sprachniveaus.
 Praxisnah vermittelst du moderne Fahrzeugtechnik, Fahrzeugdiagnose sowie Themen wie Fahrzeugelektronik, Assistenzsysteme, Bussysteme, Hochvolttechnik und Elektromobilität.
 Mit Blick auf den deutschen Arbeitsmarkt bereitest du die Teilnehmenden auf Kompetenzfeststellungen, fachliche Prüfungen und berufliche Anforderungen vor.
 Die Dokumentation von Lernfortschritten sowie die Förderung von Qualitäts-, Sicherheits-, Gesundheits- und Umweltbewusstsein runden dein Aufgabenfeld ab.
 Der Online-Unterricht wird voraussichtlich 2-mal wöchentlich nachmittags von 16:00 Uhr-17:30 Uhr , 2-mal wöchentlich abends von 18:00 Uhr - 20:30 Uhr und 1-2mal monatlich am Samstag von 8:00 Uhr - 16:15 Uhr stattfinden.
 DEINE STÄRKEN. 
 Du hast Freude daran, Menschen für Technik zu begeistern und Wissen verständlich zu vermitteln. Eine wertschätzende Haltung, pädagogisches Geschick und ein professioneller Umgang mit unterschiedlichen kulturellen Hintergründen zeichnen dich aus. Gleichzeitig arbeitest du strukturiert, verantwortungsvoll und praxisorientiert.
 Das benötigen wir
 Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung als Kfz-Mechatroniker:in oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation.
 Mehrjährige praktische Berufserfahrung in der Kfz-Mechatronik, idealerweise im Bereich PKW-Technik.
 Fundierte Kenntnisse moderner Fahrzeugtechnik, Fahrzeugdiagnose sowie in der Fahrzeugelektrik und Fahrzeugelektronik.
 Kenntnisse im Bereich Hochvoltsysteme und Elektromobilität sowie eine gültige HV-Qualifikation, idealerweise auf Niveau HV S2 oder HV S3.
 Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse sowie die Fähigkeit, komplexe technische Inhalte verständlich und praxisnah zu vermitteln.
 Das wäre schön
 Eine Ausbildereignung nach AEVO (AdA-Schein).
 Erfahrung in der beruflichen Bildung, Ausbildung oder Erwachsenenbildung.
 Kenntnisse in der fachlichen Unterweisung oder Qualifizierung im Bereich Hochvolttechnik.
 Zusätzliche Sprachkenntnisse für die Arbeit mit internationalen Teilnehmenden.
 Erfahrung im Umgang mit heterogenen Lerngruppen und unterschiedlichen Lernvoraussetzungen.
